source.title_on_document: Fostering children’s creativity through LLM-driven storytelling with a social robot

paper_design_summary: Study 1 analyzed 32 children telling stories with a tele-operated robot that supplied previously collected human story ideas; the groups were matched on pre-test creativity, age, and gender, and neither fluency nor originality differed significantly between creative and non-creative robot conditions (p. 5, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2; p. 7, Section 3.2.5). Study 2 compared creative and non-creative fine-tuned GPT-3 robot behavior in collaborative and non-collaborative storytelling conditions, analyzing 93 children (sum of the reported arm counts); coders scored the children’s fluency, flexibility, elaboration, and originality, but the text describes group balancing without stating the allocation procedure (p. 8, Sections 3.4.1-3.4.2; p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). The five extracted outcomes below concern Study 2; the intervening model-validation survey assessed model-generated stories rather than children’s creative output (p. 8, Section 3.3).

studies.label: Experiment 1: Once upon a story (tele-operated robot)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Children were split into matched groups based on creativity pre-test, age, and gender and allocated to creative or non-creative tele-operated robot behavior. This experiment used human-selected human ideas, not generative-AI assistance.
assignment.quote: We opted to split our sample into two evenly matched groups based on creativity levels, age, and gender and allocated them to either the creative or the non-creative condition.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Section 3.2.2.1 (Creativity pre-test); Section 3.2.2.2 describes selection of previously collected children’s ideas by a human tele-operator.

arms.name: Creative tele-operated robot
arms.description: Human tele-operator selected more ideas and more original ideas from a previously collected children’s storytelling dataset; analyzed arm count not reported (p. 5, Section 3.2.2.2).

arms.name: Non-creative tele-operated robot
arms.description: Human tele-operator selected fewer ideas and less original ideas from the same pool; analyzed arm count not reported (p. 5, Section 3.2.2.2).

participants.exclusions: Six children who withdrew from the activity or did not interact with the robot were excluded; 38 recruited and 32 analyzed. Exclusion timing relative to allocation is not stated (p. 5, Section 3.2.1).
participants.who: Children aged 5-10 recruited at the Museum of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden; 38 recruited and 32 analyzed after six withdrew or did not interact with the robot. Arm-specific analyzed counts are not stated.
participants.quote: Six children who either withdrew from the activity or did not interact with the robot were excluded, leaving data from 32 participants (15 males, 17 females) for analysis.

ai_tool.name_model: Tele-operated Furhat robot; no generative model used in this experiment
ai_tool.how_used: A human operator selected ideas from a previously collected human storytelling dataset and made the robot deliver them. Random selection refers to story ideas, not assignment of children (p. 5, Section 3.2.2.2).

task.description: Spoken collaborative storytelling in Swedish: the child and robot alternated story ideas while using a castle-themed touchscreen interface (p. 5, Section 3.2.2.2).
task.duration: Storytelling capped at 10 minutes; experiment typically 15-20 minutes per child (p. 5, Section 3.2.3).

studies.label: Experiment 2: CreativeBot (autonomous GPT-3 robot; allocation procedure unstated)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Children participated in one of four conditions crossing creative versus non-creative autonomous robot behavior with collaborative versus non-collaborative storytelling. The text says the groups were balanced on pre-test creativity, size, age, and gender, but does not state how children were assigned or whether assignment was random.
assignment.quote: We therefore ensured that the 4 experimental groups were balanced in terms of children’s creative abilities.
assignment.locator: p. 8, Section 3.4.2.1 (Creativity pre-test): this is the closest allocation-related statement; no explicit random or non-random assignment mechanism is given. The random assignment on p. 10, Section 3.4.4 concerns data allocated to coders.

arms.name: Creative Collaborative (CC)
arms.description: Child and creative autonomous robot alternated story ideas; analyzed count from p. 8, Section 3.4.1; behavior defined in p. 9, Table 3.

arms.name: Creative Non-Collaborative (CNC)
arms.description: Creative autonomous robot told a story first, then asked the child to tell another story; analyzed count from p. 8, Section 3.4.1; behavior defined in p. 9, Table 3.

arms.name: Non-creative Collaborative (NCC)
arms.description: Child and non-creative autonomous robot alternated story ideas; analyzed count from p. 8, Section 3.4.1; behavior defined in p. 9, Table 3.

arms.name: Non-creative Non-Collaborative (NCNC)
arms.description: Non-creative autonomous robot told a story first, then asked the child to tell another story; analyzed count from p. 8, Section 3.4.1; behavior defined in p. 9, Table 3.

participants.exclusions: 10 children were excluded because of missing data or inconsistencies in data collection. Exclusion timing relative to allocation is not stated; 103 is the recruited count, and no randomized count is reported (p. 8, Section 3.4.1).
participants.who: Children aged 7-9 from three British international schools in Stockholm, Sweden, completing the task in English. The paper reports 103 recruited and 10 excluded for missing data or inconsistent data collection; 93 analyzed is the sum of the four printed arm counts.
participants.quote: We structured our experiment into four conditions: creative collaborative (24 users), creative non-collaborative (23 users), non-creative collaborative (23 users) and non-creative non-collaborative (23 users).
participants.locator: p. 8, Section 3.4.1 (Participants). Analyzed total calculated directly from printed counts: 24 + 23 + 23 + 23 = 93, consistent with 103 recruited minus 10 excluded; not a randomized count.

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT-3 fine-tuned into creative and non-creative models, deployed on a Furhat social robot
ai_tool.how_used: An autonomous spoken storytelling partner supplied context-dependent story continuations in collaborative conditions and told a story before the child’s story in non-collaborative conditions. Models were fine-tuned using children’s story ideas labeled for creativity; no more specific GPT-3 model identifier is given (pp. 7-8, Section 3.3; pp. 8-9, Section 3.4.2.2 and Table 3).

task.description: Spoken storytelling in English using a castle-themed interface: child and robot either took turns to create a shared story or the robot told a story and then the child told another. Outcomes were scored on the child’s story contributions during the interaction (pp. 8-10, Sections 3.4.2-3.4.4 and Table 5).
task.duration: Open-ended interaction lasting 5-25 minutes, ended by the child saying "the end" (p. 10, Section 3.4.3).

outcomes.name: Fluency of story ideas (number of story elements uttered by the child)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Behavioral coders counted the story elements uttered by each child (p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). Output was assessed during the robot interaction (p. 12, Section 4).

contrasts.reported: Creative conditions (CC and CNC) versus non-creative conditions (NCC and NCNC): higher fluency; p < 0.01, Mean = 83.68, SD = 79.67. These are the labels and numbers printed in the results text; the single mean/SD pair is not explicitly identified as an arm-specific or whole-sample summary. Analysis used MANOVA after log transformation.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Section 3.4.5.1 (reported statistics), Table 5 and Section 3.4.4 (definition and behavioral coding); p. 11, Figure 5A.

contrasts.reported: Collaborative conditions (CC and NCC) versus non-collaborative conditions (CNC and NCNC): the MANOVA found no significant effect on fluency. Section 3.4.5.2 reports no significant effect on the four creativity metrics collectively; no outcome-specific exact p-value, test statistic, effect estimate, arm-specific means or SDs, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Table 5 (outcome definitions) and Section 3.4.5.2 (collaboration results).

outcomes.name: Flexibility of story ideas (number of different story-element categories)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Behavioral coders counted the different categories to which each child’s story elements belonged, such as action, time, and location. This is variety within a child’s story, not diversity across children (p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). Output was assessed during the robot interaction (p. 12, Section 4).

contrasts.reported: Creative conditions (CC and CNC) versus non-creative conditions (NCC and NCNC): higher flexibility; p < 0.05, Mean = 3.02, SD = 0.41. These are the labels and numbers printed in the results text; the single mean/SD pair is not explicitly identified as an arm-specific or whole-sample summary. Analysis used MANOVA after log transformation.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Section 3.4.5.1 (reported statistics), Table 5 and Section 3.4.4 (definition and behavioral coding); p. 11, Figure 5B.

contrasts.reported: Collaborative conditions (CC and NCC) versus non-collaborative conditions (CNC and NCNC): the MANOVA found no significant effect on flexibility. Section 3.4.5.2 reports no significant effect on the four creativity metrics collectively; no outcome-specific exact p-value, test statistic, effect estimate, arm-specific means or SDs, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Table 5 (outcome definitions) and Section 3.4.5.2 (collaboration results).

outcomes.name: Elaboration of story details (word count minus story-element count)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Behavioral coders measured the difference between each child’s word count and story-element count (p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). Output was assessed during the robot interaction (p. 12, Section 4).

contrasts.reported: Creative conditions (CC and CNC) versus non-creative conditions (NCC and NCNC): greater elaboration; p < 0.05, Mean = 88.45, SD = 87.7. These are the labels and numbers printed in the results text; the single mean/SD pair is not explicitly identified as an arm-specific or whole-sample summary. Analysis used MANOVA after log transformation.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Section 3.4.5.1 (reported statistics), Table 5 and Section 3.4.4 (definition and behavioral coding); p. 11, Figure 5C.

contrasts.reported: Collaborative conditions (CC and NCC) versus non-collaborative conditions (CNC and NCNC): the MANOVA found no significant effect on elaboration. Section 3.4.5.2 reports no significant effect on the four creativity metrics collectively; no outcome-specific exact p-value, test statistic, effect estimate, arm-specific means or SDs, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Table 5 (outcome definitions) and Section 3.4.5.2 (collaboration results).

outcomes.name: Average originality of story ideas
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Behavioral coders rated each story idea on a scale from 1 to 3 for surprise and novelty; the child-level score is the average originality of all that child’s ideas (p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). Output was assessed during the robot interaction (p. 12, Section 4). Figure 5D concerns frequency of medium-originality ideas, not this average score.

contrasts.reported: The paper reports no significant effect of the robot’s creativity level on children’s average originality. No exact p-value, arm-specific means or SDs, effect estimate, or confidence interval is supplied for this contrast. Analysis used MANOVA after log transformation.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4 (scoring), Section 3.4.5.1, Originality bullet (result).

contrasts.reported: Collaborative conditions (CC and NCC) versus non-collaborative conditions (CNC and NCNC): the MANOVA found no significant effect on average originality. Section 3.4.5.2 reports no significant effect on the four creativity metrics collectively; no outcome-specific exact p-value, test statistic, effect estimate, arm-specific means or SDs, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Table 5 (outcome definitions) and Section 3.4.5.2 (collaboration results).

outcomes.name: Frequency of medium-originality story ideas (level 2)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count within each child’s story of ideas rated level 2 on the 1-to-3 originality scale by behavioral coders. This outcome counts moderately original ideas rather than averaging originality ratings; it does not measure diversity across children (p. 10, Table 5, Sections 3.4.4 and 3.4.5.1; p. 11, Figure 5D). Output was assessed during the robot interaction (p. 12, Section 4).

contrasts.reported: Creative conditions (CC and CNC) versus non-creative conditions (NCC and NCNC): more medium originality level ideas (level 2 on a scale from 1 to 3); p < 0.05, Mean = 2.68, SD = 3.27. The single mean/SD pair is not explicitly identified as an arm-specific or whole-sample summary. Analysis used MANOVA after log transformation. Figure 5D plots this frequency, not average originality.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 (conditions); p. 10, Section 3.4.5.1, Originality bullet; p. 11, Figure 5D.

eligibility.reason: Study 2 compares generative-AI configurations and analyzes 93 children (24 + 23 + 23 + 23; p. 8, Section 3.4.1), with creativity scored on their story output (p. 10, Table 5 and Section 3.4.4). Its group-balancing description does not establish random assignment or another explicit allocation mechanism (p. 8, Section 3.4.2.1), so criterion 1 and core eligibility remain unclear. The random assignment mentioned in Section 3.4.4 concerns recordings assigned to coders, not children assigned to conditions (p. 10). Study 1 describes matched groups without explicitly stating whether assignment was random, analyzes only 32 children, and uses human-selected human story ideas rather than generative AI (p. 5, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2); it cannot qualify. Neither study supplies an AI-versus-human-output comparison or a confirmed non-random generative-AI comparison, so context_class remains none.

one_line_finding: Children in the creative GPT-3 robot conditions showed higher fluency (p < 0.01), flexibility and elaboration (both p < 0.05), but no significant difference in average originality (p. 10, Section 3.4.5.1); random allocation of children is not stated (p. 8, Section 3.4.2.1).
notes: The data_url points to the story-idea dataset and its creativity ratings used for fine-tuning the models (p. 3, footnote 3); the paper does not establish that this repository contains the analyzed Study 2 participant data. The Data availability statement instead says that raw data supporting the conclusions will be made available by the authors (p. 13). The collaboration result is recorded for the four Table 5 metrics; Section 3.4.5.2 does not separately report a collaboration contrast for the frequency of medium-originality ideas.
